Consider the region $R$ shown above. Let the function $f(x,y)$ be defined as

$$
f(x,y)={\begin{aligned}y\operatorname{cos}⁡x, & (x,y)\in S, \\ 0, & (x,y)\in T, \\ {e}^{x+y}, & (x,y)\in U.\end{aligned}
$$

Then,

$$
{∬}_{R}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A=
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that the domain $R$ can be represented as a union of three sub-domains, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}R & =S\cup T\cup U.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{S}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{T}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{U}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{S}y\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{T}0\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{U}{e}^{x+y}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{S}y\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{U}{e}^{x+y}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

The source's exact set-union equality incorrectly omits the line y=2, where the problem also leaves f undefined. Defining f arbitrarily on that measure-zero line preserves the integral and the selected answer. q-81253: the cosine contribution is zero and the other contribution is (3/2)(2)=3; the source has a harmless duplicated equals sign. q-129184: 2z=x²+y². q-36464: z=sqrt(x²+y²), selecting the upper cone.
